title: HINT for Compliance — controls keep their evidence
metaDescription: Keep frameworks, controls, owners, evidence and exceptions together so assistants draft compliance work without inventing regulations.
h1: Your assistant drafts controls fast. HINT keeps every claim tied to evidence.
intro: HINT keeps frameworks, control owners, evidence and exceptions in plain-text notes beside compliance documents. Your assistant reads the rules for the business unit before it drafts or maps a control.

situations.before: A control sounds complete but nobody owns it.
situations.after: Ownership is part of the control
situations.body: The responsible role, cadence and evidence expectation remain attached instead of disappearing into polished prose.

situations.before: An exception becomes an undocumented permanent practice.
situations.body: The assistant sees the boundary, approver and review date whenever it works on the affected unit.

situations.before: A framework requirement is quoted from memory.
situations.body: Missing authority is flagged for compliance review rather than turned into a confident citation.

example.intro: The Wonka compliance demo keeps the factory control grounded in SRC-1.
example.after: It drafts the control with its declared source and asks for any missing owner, evidence or cadence before presenting the record as complete.
example.compiled:
<control name="overview-1">
  Approved control grounded in SRC-1.
</control>
<source name="SRC-1">../../sources/approved.md</source>

never: Invent a regulation, clause number or control requirement.
Treat an exception without approval and expiry as permanent policy.
Claim operating effectiveness without declared evidence.
disclaimer: HINT supports compliance documentation, not legal interpretation or certification. Qualified reviewers decide applicability and effectiveness.

faq.a: No. It keeps requirements, controls and evidence expectations connected; assurance still depends on actual operation and review.

faq.q: Can it map more than one framework?
faq.a: Yes. Framework and requirement blocks can share controls while retaining distinct sources and applicability.

faq.q: Can auditors use the same repository?
faq.a: Yes. Compliance and audit books can coexist, with the task-specific vocabulary ordered first.

keywordDescriptions.framework: Names a compliance framework and its applicability.
keywordDescriptions.requirement: Records a sourced obligation from the framework.
keywordDescriptions.unit: Sets the organizational scope a rule applies to.
keywordDescriptions.control: Defines an owned action intended to address a requirement.
keywordDescriptions.evidence: Names the artifact that demonstrates control operation.
keywordDescriptions.mapping: Connects controls to the requirements they address.
keywordDescriptions.exception: Records an approved deviation, owner and expiry.
keywordDescriptions.redflag: Marks a condition that requires escalation.
